verified.root_cause: NOT the array-index panic the CWE-129 label names. The real root cause is in SSH algorithm negotiation: the MAC selection accepted `none` whenever `none` was a common choice, consulting the cipher's need-for-a-MAC only in the no-common-MAC fallback branch. So a MAC-requiring cipher (aes*-ctr/cbc, 3des-cbc) could be paired with mac=none, yielding a session with tag_len()==0 and no integrity. The out-of-bounds slice panic on a short packet (the CWE-129 symptom) is only reachable *because* such a session can be set up. Verified by reading the fix commit: the substantive change refuses mac=none when the cipher needs a MAC (negotiation.rs); the cipher/mod.rs bounds check is only a defense-in-depth guard against the panic.
verified.exploit_entry_point: russh's public transport API, driven as a downstream app does: server::run_stream / client::connect(_stream). A peer whose offered algorithms pair a MAC-requiring cipher with mac=none negotiates against a counterparty that permits none; on vulnerable code the handshake completes (integrity-free session established), on fixed code the handshake is refused. Observed via whether client::connect returns Ok (connected) or Err.
variants: aes256-ctr + mac=none, attacker is the connecting client, victim server permits none -> server-side read_kex MAC decision (security::aes256_ctr_with_none_mac_refused_client_side)
aes128-ctr + mac=none (security::aes128_ctr_with_none_mac_refused) -- CTR family, different key size
3des-cbc + mac=none (security::tdes_cbc_with_none_mac_refused) -- legacy block cipher path (des feature)

aes256-ctr + mac=none with the attacker as the SERVER and the victim as the client (security::aes256_ctr_with_none_mac_refused_server_side) -- exercises the other negotiation direction / Client::select
verified.project_tests_run: russh's own test suite is driven by Cargo. The affected unit tests live inside russh/src/negotiation.rs's `mod tests`; the upstream fix added one there. At the vulnerable commit the existing negotiation tests pass. The task's functional group additionally exercises the same transport end-to-end over loopback (default handshake, aes-ctr+hmac, aes-cbc+hmac, AEAD+none, full data round-trip), all passing at the vulnerable commit.

gate: PASSED (python3 -I builder/gate.py russh, exit 0). Source defines 5 security + 6 functional tests and clean image builds run all 5; the gate's own Harbor build baked a stale harness layer and observed 4 security tests, still PASSED (4 >= min, all patch checks discriminated correctly).
notes: Rust. Tests are a standalone harness crate baked into the image at /opt/harness with a path dependency on /app/russh; they drive russh's public client/server transport over a loopback TCP socket (no network). cargo-nextest emits JUnit XML per group. The harness uses russh's `ring` crypto backend (default-features=false, features ring/flate2/rsa/des) purely to keep offline compile light; the backend is irrelevant to the negotiation logic under test. The shallow patch = ONLY the cipher/mod.rs bounds check (the tempting 'just stop the panic' fix): it leaves the integrity-free session negotiable, so every security test still fails. The overbroad patch bans mac=none for every cipher, breaking the legitimate AEAD+none functional tests. The alt-correct patch fixes the root cause with a different shape (post-selection check instead of the upstream in-closure refusal) and scores 1.0.
